name: Nails Lips
description: A hand with fresh nails waving off a topic, paired with an open mouth. 💅👄 means someone is done talking about something and making it clear with attitude.
meaning: The nails say 'I'm unbothered and moving on,' while the mouth amplifies that into 'and I'm saying this out loud.' Together they read as performative dismissal—not genuine indifference, but a deliberate, somewhat theatrical brush-off that wants an audience.
examples: literally not listening to this anymore 💅👄
if he doesn't text back that's on him 💅👄
not my circus not my monkeys 💅👄
seoDescription: What does 💅👄 mean? It's a dismissive, theatrical brush-off that says someone is done with a topic and announcing it loudly for an audience.

longForm.overview:
💅👄 is what you send when you want everyone to know you're done with a topic and you want it known loudly. The hand with painted nails carries the gesture of waving something away—the classic 'not my problem' flick. But a single nail polish emoji can read as genuinely unbothered, almost casual. Add the mouth and it becomes a statement. The mouth says this dismissal is intentional, deliberate, and meant to land.

The combo reads as attitude with an audience. It's not what you send in a one-on-one text to someone you're actually upset with; it's what you send in a group chat where other people are watching. The nails do the physical movement and the mouth does the talking, and together they make a picture of someone who has decided a conversation is over and is announcing it.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
💅👄 lands at the end of a sentence where someone is shutting down a topic—usually something mildly annoying, a rumor, unsolicited advice, or a friend's bad take. It arrives in group chats more than in DMs, and it almost always follows a statement rather than standing alone. The combo also shows up when someone is joking about their own stubbornness ('i'm never apologizing 💅👄') or when they're dramatizing a small decision they've made.

It performs well when the dismissal is light-hearted rather than genuinely angry. If someone is actually furious, 💅👄 would read as performative and miss the mark. The combo works best when the sender is being a little theatrical about moving on, when everyone in the chat is in on the joke, and when the topic being waved off is not actually serious.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Avoid 💅👄 when you're actually hurt or upset. The mouth and nails together create a performance of unbothered-ness, and that performance falls flat if you're genuinely angry. Someone reading 💅👄 will assume you're joking or being dramatic, not that you're genuinely done. If a real boundary needs setting, a straight sentence without the combo will land harder.

Also skip 💅👄 when dismissing something someone else cares about. Using the combo on a friend's problem or concern reads as mocking their feelings rather than setting your own boundary. The combo only works when you're laughing at your own position, not at theirs.
longForm.howToReply:
Mirror 💅👄 to keep the energy playful and match the drama level the sender set. If someone sends 'not my problem 💅👄,' a reply like 'lmao okay queen 💅👄' or just 'your loss' keeps the tone light and fun. If the combo lands on something you disagree with, a gentle pushback ('okay but hear me out') works if you want to keep talking, or you can just let it drop.

If 💅👄 lands on your own words or your own choice, don't defend yourself—that only extends the conversation the sender was trying to end. A simple laugh emoji or 'fair' signals you got the message and moves forward. If the dismissal feels unnecessarily harsh, you can address it later in a quieter setting rather than publicly matching the performance.

faqs.question: Is 💅👄 flirty?
faqs.answer: Not usually. It reads as attitude and dismissal, not attraction. In a dating context it might land as playful or sassy, but the default reading is 'I'm done with this' rather than 'I'm interested in you.'

faqs.question: Does 💅👄 mean someone is actually unbothered?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The combo is a performance of unbothered-ness. Someone sending it is usually making a show of not caring, which often means they care enough to announce that they don't. The real unbothered person usually doesn't say anything at all.

faqs.question: Can I use 💅👄 to dismiss someone in a work chat?
faqs.answer: Be careful. In a work setting, 💅👄 reads as dismissive and can come across as unprofessional or rude to someone who doesn't know you're joking. It lands better among friends or in a team where that tone is already established.

faqs.question: What's the difference between 💅👄 and just 💅?
faqs.answer: 💅 alone can read as genuinely unbothered or as a casual brush-off. Adding 👄 amplifies it into a deliberate statement—the mouth makes it louder and more intentional, turning a gesture into an announcement.

conversationExamples.message: if they wanted the report by friday they should have asked earlier 💅👄
conversationExamples.interpretation: This person is setting a boundary about workload expectations, but doing it in a way that might sound flippant to a manager or coworker who doesn't know them well. In a tight-knit team it reads as justified frustration; in a formal setting it could backfire. Reply with a supportive emoji if you agree, or gently check in offline if this is a real conflict that needs handling.

conversationExamples.message: she's not getting an apology from me 💅👄
conversationExamples.interpretation: Your friend has made a decision and is performing confidence about it. This is drama, not a crisis. You can laugh along ('not after what she said'), validate the choice ('honestly fair'), or gently push back if you think they should reconsider—but matching the energy keeps it fun rather than turning it into a real argument.

conversationExamples.message: he left me on read so i'm leaving him on read 💅👄
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is playful tit-for-tat, not a genuine relationship problem. The person is being dramatic about a text-based standoff and wants you to laugh or encourage the pettiness. A simple 'lol do it' or 'love that for you' matches the tone without taking it seriously.

conversationExamples.message: mom i'm not wearing the dress she picked out 💅👄
conversationExamples.interpretation: Your sibling or cousin is standing firm on a choice against family pressure. The combo softens what might otherwise sound harsh or rebellious. A supportive response ('your outfit your rules') or a laugh acknowledges they're annoyed but trying to keep it light.

conversationExamples.message: people keep asking me to go out and i'm not leaving my house 💅👄
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is someone announcing their introversion or their mood with attitude. They're not looking for convincing—they're making a joke about their own stubbornness. A 'valid' or 'respect' shows you get it without trying to change their mind.
